_comment: Canon for every performance ratio quoted on the marketing site's high-traffic surfaces (homepage sections, page.tsx, layout.tsx metadata + JSON-LD). Same contract as commercial-terms.json: change this file first, then propagate. CI enforces it via tests/test_site_claims.py — a ratio on those surfaces that is not listed here fails the build. This exists because the site drifted: it carried a 65.6x figure attributed to three different repo sizes, a 63.6x typo of the same number, a 0.81s latency with no source in the repo, a '100% gold-file recall' that the current public benchmark contradicts (93.75% mean), and the real name of a private client whose field report the docs deliberately anonymize.

_evidence_levels.ci-gated: Recomputed and asserted on every PR. Cannot silently regress.
_evidence_levels.reproducible: Not a gate, but any reader can rerun it from a fresh clone and get the same number on the same machine. Token counts, and the ratios built on them, can shift slightly from one machine to another; where that has been measured, recall-type figures did not move, and the source page states the token spread (docs/benchmarks/public.md: per-repo mean tokens within 1.3% across CI runners; recall, found-rate and MRR identical on every machine compared).
_evidence_levels.field-report: One repo, one developer, maintainer-measured. Reproducible in method, not in number. Must be labelled as such wherever it appears.
_evidence_levels.community: Submitted to docs/community-benchmarks.json by a named submitter. n is small; treat as directional.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: 93.75% gold-file recall (mean over all 40 queries, query-weighted), 85-100% per repo, 90% found-rate, across 40 pre-registered queries on 4 pinned OSS repos
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: Do NOT round this to '100% recall'. Per-repo recall is 0.93 / 1.00 / 0.85 / 1.00 (requests / click / flask / rich); flask is the weakest and every miss (4 of 40) is published. The mean is query-weighted (37.5 of 40 gold-file hits); the unweighted average of the per-repo means is 94.5% and is not the figure we quote. Backed by bench/public/results.json, regenerated 2026-09-27 at v4.3.4 — tests/test_site_claims.py recomputes the mean and per-repo ratios from that file.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: Synapse recall never lowers top-k hit rate, at a neutral token budget
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: The CI gate is DIRECTIONAL: test_synapse_recall_does_not_reduce_hit_rate asserts on >= off, and test_synapse_recall_is_budget_neutral bounds the reduction delta. It does not gate a magnitude. The +6.1 pts (77.2% -> 83.3%) figure published in docs/wiki/ traces to the v0.25.0 2x2 study; the self-benchmark's current Phase 2 output reports +3.5 pts (74.6% -> 78.1%). Do not quote either magnitude as 'CI-gated' — quote the gate, and let the reproduction command give the number. HISTORY: this gate measured -1.75 pts (74.6% -> 72.8%) on AVX-512 hosts and +3.5 elsewhere, bit-stably, for months. A 2-point tolerance was added 2026-08-29 to make it pass and was reverted; the cause was displacement dropping the ranked tail, which could evict a module's only representatives. Fixed 2026-08-31 by choosing displacement victims whose module another survivor still covers. Both host classes now measure +3.51 on this fixture (74.6% -> 78.1%), verified on an avx512f container and a non-avx512f CI runner at the same commit.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: Faithfulness vs naive truncation at a matched token budget: CI fails if the mean delta falls below -0.10 (built-in backend, mean of 3 runs on the reference fixture). At v4.3.4 it measures -0.054 — naive truncation keeps slightly more gold facts — and the site publishes that as a loss.
non_ratio_headline_claims.note: Do NOT describe this as 'never worse' or 'beats truncation'. ci-benchmark.yml asserts mean_faithfulness_delta >= -0.10, not >= 0.0: the gate was relaxed because sample_project mixes code with prose chapter summaries, where a matched-budget naive baseline can edge out the built-in backend. CI output on #539: built-in recall 0.451 vs naive 0.505, delta runs [-0.054, -0.054, -0.054]. Earlier releases measured +0.013 to +0.143. Quote the gate and the current, dated measurement; re-check both whenever ci-benchmark.yml or the fixture changes.

non_ratio_headline_claims.claim: TurboVec fact recall 0.800 vs chroma float32 0.744, identical top-k hit@4

unsourced_do_not_use.why: No measurement anywhere in the repo produces this number. There is per-query latency instrumentation (neuralmind/metrics_pipeline.py) but no committed benchmark result, so the figure cannot be defended. Speed claims must be mechanism-based ('a local index lookup, not another model call') until a latency benchmark is committed.
A transcription error for the 65.6x community submission. There is no 63.6x measurement.
Matches no repo in any dataset. 65.6x came from a 241-node repo; the 1,626-node repo measured 46.0x; the field report repo has ~9,300 nodes.

unsourced_do_not_use.claim: 100% gold-file recall on the public benchmark
unsourced_do_not_use.why: Contradicted by the current public benchmark: 0.93 on requests, 0.85 on flask. The 100% figure came from an older, narrower competitor eval that the docs already flag as not re-verified against the expanded corpus.

Both CI gates assert direction only (on >= off, delta >= 0.0), never a magnitude, and both published magnitudes are contradicted by current CI output. Quoting a number as gated when only its sign is gated is the same defect as quoting a number with no measurement at all.

Superseded 2026-09-27. Published 2026-09-16 from a re-run whose raw output was never committed (bench/public/results.json still held an older run), and '93.6%' was the unweighted average of per-repo means labelled as a weighted mean. The committed run at v4.3.4 measures 93.75% (query-weighted), 4 misses, 45-261x.

_attribution_rule: A ratio is only correct together with the repo it was measured on and the evidence level it carries. The original defect was not a wrong number — 65.6 is a real measurement — it was that number bolted to a '1,486-node production codebase' that appears in no dataset. So entries that were measured on a specific repo declare `nodes`, and tests/test_site_claims.py checks the (ratio, node-count) pair and the claimed evidence level wherever the site states them, not just the numeric value.
